gaps: The draft does not define how a Claude session selects the new hybrid transport or when it falls back to the plugin. The current selector in factory/scripts/forge_cli/codex_runtime.py chooses only the coordinator (`claude` or `codex`), while factory/scripts/forge_cli/delegate.py launches the plugin for Claude.

The startup check lacks an exact SDK version, compatible Codex binary version, installation path, and upgrade rule. factory/scripts/forge_cli/doctor.py currently checks a CLI minimum and the installed plugin, but does not install or check `openai-codex`.

The warm story thread has no specified creation point, read-only policy, source revision, or freshness rule. After a dependency merges or a decision changes, a later task could fork context that predates its approved contract; docs/decisions/0059-task-owned-jit-workspaces.md requires task planning against completed dependency state.

The task fork has no stated point after its JIT plan, cold grill, and native approval, nor a rule for supplying the final task brief and preserving the delegated Sol/medium lead and Luna/max edit roles. See WORKFLOW.md's task sequence and docs/decisions/0084-delegated-thread-leads-on-sol-medium.md.

A review-fix resume must still pass `forge delegate`'s current task, stage, brief, effective or narrowed scope, and triage checks. The draft does not bind the recorded thread and each resumed turn to that fresh preparation or say what happens when any binding has changed; see factory/scripts/forge_cli/delegate.py:cmd_delegate.

“Diff since the thread's base” does not define the base commit, whether staged, unstaged, and untracked changes are included, or how the diff is bounded after compaction and multiple fix rounds. The proof boundary uses the task stage base and current product delta; see factory/scripts/forge_cli/stages.py and docs/QUALITY.md.

The event-stream requirement does not specify reconnect, missed events, duplicate events, turn failure, or loss of the supervising process. It also lacks a terminal-state check preventing a live or unknown worker from writing while `forge task close` measures and seals the tree; see WORKFLOW.md's close sequence.

A raised signal currently tells the worker to pause until the orchestrator records a resolution (factory/scripts/forge_cli/signal.py:cmd_raise and cmd_resolve). The draft does not define how Forge identifies the exact active turn, confirms the pause, handles a signal near turn completion, or delivers the recorded answer before execution continues.

The proposed approval handler has no specified fail-closed implementation. The SDK's high-level `Codex` constructor exposes no approval handler, while its lower-level `CodexClient` defaults command and file approval requests to `accept`; the draft must name the integration that overrides that default on every path. [SDK API](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/sdk/python/src/openai_codex/api.py), [SDK client](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/sdk/python/src/openai_codex/client.py).

The thread ledger has no authoritative location, atomic recorder/retry rules, or binding from thread ID to story, task worktree, Git common directory, approved contract, stage incarnation, and current delegation. A thread ID and fork parent alone cannot reject a copied, stale, or cross-task resume; compare factory/schemas/delegation.json and factory/scripts/forge_cli/worker_admission.py.

“One app-server” does not define the lock's repository identity, ownership check, fencing, crash recovery, or behavior when another Codex client resumes a persisted thread. A process-local claim alone cannot establish acceptance criterion 5.

Story-close archival lacks a named close event, ordering relative to task markers and story outcome, handling of still-active turns, retry after partial archival, and a rule for a reopened story. Archiving retains a stored thread, so acceptance criterion 6 also needs to define what “rollout never outlives its story” means.

The primary-checkout approval path does not specify how an authentic host event selects exactly one task worktree and rechecks that worktree's plan digest, frontier, and state. factory/scripts/post_tool_use.py calls `record_native_approval(repo_root(), ...)`, and factory/scripts/forge_cli/approval.py derives candidates from that root's worktree-local run state.

Acceptance criterion 1 has no reproducible benchmark: it omits the cold control, same-fix equivalence, measurement boundary, repetitions, and treatment of token or wall-time variance. One faster observation would not establish the promised improvement.

Acceptance criterion 8 names only existing dual-runtime parity checks. It lacks proof for the new hybrid route across setup, init/adopt/upgrade, supported platforms, scoped writes, fallback, hook delivery, and task close; docs/specs/dual-coordinator-parity.md requires real adapter and platform evidence rather than a CLI smoke check.
contradictions: The draft says Claude delegations use a Forge-owned app-server while the plugin is merely fallback, but docs/product/BRIEF.md, docs/architecture/dual-coordinator-parity.md, and docs/specs/delegation-boundary.md bind Claude writes to the admitted `codex-plugin-cc` companion and its launch/cleanup proof. The spec names no replacement authority or change to those accepted contracts.

The claim that per-task scopes and proof remain unchanged cannot hold with one shared app-server process as described. Claude admission currently binds a per-launch process token, PID ancestry, held task lock, and starting/running rows, and stage close requires a successful companion launch (factory/scripts/forge_cli/worker_admission.py:live_worker_admission; factory/scripts/forge_cli/stages.py:_stage_write_launch_valid). The draft supplies no equivalent per-turn admission or close proof.

“Workers run with approvals on request” conflicts with the accepted `approval_policy="never"` for Forge-managed Codex chats in docs/decisions/0081-full-access-for-forge-managed-codex-chats.md and the committed .codex/config.toml. That policy change needs an explicit decision and corresponding trust-boundary update.

Acceptance criterion 4 treats the SDK approval round-trip as a pre-execution check for every out-of-scope command or file change. On-request approval is a sandbox escalation mechanism; operations allowed by the chosen sandbox need not request approval. The current scope boundary is the hooks and measured diff (factory/scripts/pre_tool_use.py; docs/specs/dual-coordinator-parity.md), so the stated guarantee does not follow from the proposed mechanism. [SDK sandbox reference](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/sdk/python/docs/api-reference.md).

The draft promises a plugin fallback yet acceptance criterion 9 says an SDK/app-server version mismatch refuses instead of running. It does not distinguish a safe pre-dispatch fallback from a refusal after a thread or worker may already have acted.

Using the host's project directory to locate hooks contradicts docs/decisions/0038-portable-fail-closed-hooks.md, which explicitly rejected `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` as ambiguous across worktrees. Both committed hook configurations invoke the `forge` under `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`; changing that lookup without a task-worktree binding can route a gate to the primary checkout.

artifact_delta.cold:
- Hybrid-mode delegations go through a Forge-owned Codex app-server driven by the official Python
  SDK, pinned to the installed `codex` binary. The codex-plugin-cc companion remains the fallback;
  native Codex coordination and Claude-only mode are unchanged. `forge delegate` stays the single
  entry point, and per-task worktrees, scopes, proof and review are unchanged.
- Each task keeps its Codex worker thread. A review-fix round resumes that thread with the current
  commit, the diff since the thread's base, and the triaged findings, instead of starting a new one.
- A story keeps one warm thread that has read the story's plan, decomposition and contracts. Each
  task's worker starts as a persisted fork of it, working in the task's own worktree. Threads are
  compacted between tasks and archived when the story closes.
- Forge follows every worker through the app-server event stream (items, diffs, token use, turn
  completion). A worker signal steers or interrupts the running turn instead of cancelling it.
- Workers run with approvals on request. A write or command outside the task's scope is asked
  about, and Forge answers it against the task's write scope before it happens. Sandbox and approval
  settings are set explicitly on every turn; nothing is auto-accepted.
- Only one Forge-owned app-server holds a repository's threads at a time, so a thread is never
  claimed by two processes.
- Hooks locate the repository through the host's project directory (falling back to the git
  top-level) and record task-scoped approvals and gates against the active task's worktree, so the
  coordinator can approve and supervise a task from the primary checkout.
artifact_delta.final:
### Executor modes (decision 0085)
- `FORGE_EXECUTOR` (in `.envrc`) selects `hybrid` (default: Claude coordinates, Codex executes),
  `codex` (only Codex writes) or `claude` (Claude only; no Codex needed). It is independent of the
  existing `FORGE_COORDINATOR` (`claude`|`codex`), which keeps choosing the coordinating runtime.
- `claude` mode admits the Claude session and its subagents as writers under the same task, scope,
  proof and review gates; its cold grill uses a fresh Claude reader and Autoreview's claude engine.

### The SDK route (hybrid mode, Claude coordinating)
- A new decision (0086) makes the Forge-owned SDK route the primary Claude→Codex delegation route in
  hybrid mode and amends the delegation-boundary spec, the dual-coordinator parity architecture and the
  product brief accordingly; the codex-plugin-cc companion becomes the fallback. Native Codex
  coordination (host subagents) is unchanged.
- Route selection happens once, before dispatch, in `forge delegate`: the SDK route is used when
  `forge doctor`'s SDK check passes; otherwise the plugin route is used and the reason is printed.
  Once a thread or turn has started, there is no fallback: a failure is reported and the delegation
  is recorded as failed, never retried on another route.
- The SDK is pinned: `openai-codex` at an exact version recorded in the harness, driving the
  installed `codex` binary through `CodexConfig.codex_bin` (never the SDK's bundled binary). `forge
  doctor` checks the SDK version, the binary version against the SDK's minimum, and the path; a
  mismatch selects the plugin route pre-dispatch and names both versions.
- Admission and close proof are per turn: every delegated turn is admitted by a ledger row binding
  thread id, turn id, story, task, stage incarnation, delegation id, task worktree (and its Git common
  directory), approved contract digest and base commit. The existing worker-admission and
  stage-close checks accept an SDK row as equivalent to a companion launch row; a stage closes only
  when its last turn reached a terminal `turn/completed` state and no turn of that task is loaded.
- The SDK's approval handler is overridden on every path with an explicit handler that declines;
  with `approval_policy="never"` no approval request is expected, and any request is declined and
  logged.

### Resuming the worker for fix rounds
- Each task records its worker thread. A review-fix round runs `forge delegate` exactly as today
  (current task, stage, brief, effective scope, triage checks) and then resumes the recorded thread
  with a turn that carries: the fresh brief, the current HEAD, the committed diff from the stage base
  to HEAD plus the worktree's uncommitted changes, and the triaged findings.
- If any binding changed (task, stage incarnation, worktree, contract digest), or the thread is
  missing, archived or compacted past its base, Forge starts a new thread instead and says why.
- The delegated thread keeps its Sol/medium lead; edits go to Luna/max subagents (decision 0084).

### Live events and steering
- Forge consumes the event stream of every delegated turn (items, diff updates, token usage, turn
  completion) and writes progress to the delegation log it already watches. If the supervising
  process loses the stream, it reattaches and reconciles with `thread/read`; duplicate events are
  idempotent; a turn whose state cannot be established blocks close as "unknown", never as done.
- A worker signal pauses the worker as today; Forge maps the recorded resolution to `turn/steer` on
  the exact active turn (by turn id), or `turn/interrupt` plus a resumed turn when steering is not
  possible. A signal that arrives after the turn completed is delivered in the next resumed turn.

### One app-server, one owner
- One Forge-owned app-server per repository (keyed by the Git common directory) holds all Forge
  threads. Ownership is a lease file in the Git common directory with pid, process start time and a
  fencing counter; a stale lease (dead process) is detected and cleared; a live foreign holder is
  reported, never raced.

### Upgrade and cleanup
- `forge upgrade` of an existing client: adds the pinned SDK requirement and the doctor check, keeps
  the plugin route working, sets no `FORGE_EXECUTOR` (default `hybrid`), and changes nothing about
  in-flight tasks: a task started on the plugin route finishes on it. Re-running the upgrade is a
  no-op. The Lean client-upgrade hold must be lifted before this ships to clients.
- Cleanup: a task's worker thread is archived when its PR merges (task marker on trunk); remaining
  Forge threads are archived when the story's outcome is recorded; archival is idempotent and retried
  by `forge doctor`. The app-server lease is released on shutdown. `forge doctor --prune-threads`
  removes archived rollouts of Forge-owned threads only (by the ledger's thread ids), never the
  user's own Codex threads.

1. A review-fix round resumes the task's recorded worker thread; the resumed turn carries HEAD and

6. Threads are archived at story close; a thread's rollout never outlives its story without a record.
7. A task plan approved in native Plan Mode from the primary checkout records against the task's

1. `FORGE_EXECUTOR` selects hybrid, codex or claude as decision 0085 describes; claude mode passes

2. In hybrid mode with a passing doctor check, `forge delegate` runs the task on the SDK route; with a
   failing check it runs on the plugin route pre-dispatch and prints why; after dispatch there is no
   route fallback.
3. The SDK and binary versions are pinned and checked; a mismatch names both versions.
4. Every SDK turn is admitted by a ledger row with the bindings above, recorded through a

5. A review-fix round resumes the task's recorded thread with the fresh brief, HEAD, stage-base diff

6. Benchmark: for three recorded fix rounds, replaying the same findings on a cold delegation and on
   a resumed thread (same model, effort and brief, three runs each, median), the resumed round uses

8. A worker signal resolution reaches the exact active turn by steer or interrupt-and-resume, never

11. Worker threads are archived at task merge and story outcome; pruning touches Forge-owned threads
